Narrative statements without a case label are not assigned to individual cases: one male and two females, dorsal versus transhepatic access, prone versus left-side positioning, one patient with adrenal venous sampling (b00009), one patient with weakness, hypotension and acute adrenal insufficiency treated with hydrocortisone for 28 months (b00019, b00031), 2 weeks of hydrocortisone for one of the two other patients, one patient with improved blood pressure control, one patient with normalization of blood glucose, and the cortisol-response paragraph (b00021) with its persistent MACS and planned repeat dexamethasone suppression test and possible repeat CT. Table 1 maps acute adrenal insufficiency and bilateral adenomas only to Case 1 and the b00021 values match table cells, but because the text names no case these appear only in ambiguities and here, not as patient facts.

Series-level statistics (mean age 65 years, tumor sizes 14 to 28 mm with mean 15.75 mm, mean follow-up 15.7 months, mean hospital stay 9.3 days, average weight reduction 6 kg) are cohort statements and are not copied to individuals; the stated tumor size range does not match the smaller lesions listed in Table 1 (6x9 mm and 7x11 mm).

Methods wording on technique (patient positioning, 14-gauge antenna through 2 mm incisions, ultrasonography and CT guidance, control CT) and on the guideline-based work-up (plasma metanephrines, aldosterone-to-renin ratio) does not say it applied to each patient, so it is not recorded as patient facts. The text says histological confirmation was unnecessary; no histology is recorded.
The table prints N/A in some cells without defining it; no reason is inferred.
Values printed inside the guideline flow-charts (Fig. 1 and Fig. 3) are pixel content only and are not patient facts.
Written informed consent is stated for all participants and retrospective study design is stated; neither is recorded as a patient fact.
No supplements are listed in the source.
